- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- frontend-typescript-tailwind: Use this agent when you need to develop frontend applications or components using TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui. This includes creating React components, implementing UI designs, setting up frontend projects, refactoring existing frontend code to follow best practices, or solving frontend-specific issues. The agent specializes in modern frontend development patterns and component-based architecture.

  Context: The user needs to create a new React component with TypeScript and Tailwind.
  user: "Create a card component that displays user information"

  <commentary>
  Since the user is asking for frontend component creation, use the frontend-typescript-tailwind agent to ensure TypeScript types, Tailwind classes, and shadcn/ui patterns are properly implemented.

</example>

  <commentary>

  </commentary>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:vercel-functions: Vercel Functions expert guidance — Serverless Functions, Edge Functions, Fluid Compute, streaming, Cron Jobs, and runtime configuration. Use when configuring, debugging, or optimizing server-side code running on Vercel.

- vercel:workflow: Vercel Workflow DevKit (WDK) expert guidance. Use when building durable workflows, long-running tasks, API routes or agents that need pause/resume, retries, step-based execution, or crash-safe orchestration with Vercel Workflow.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Plan: Connector authz/identity plug-in (clean cut) + chat L1 (Telegram etc.)
2	
3	## Context (verified against origin/main code)
4	
5	### Today
6	- Generic ACL engine exists: `buildAccessGraph` → `$resource` + `member_of`, `authz_source_acl_state` (not-graphed / enforced full+fresh / stale fail-closed), channel + resource visibility compilers.
7	- **Hardcoded allowlists** (not auto-discovery from connectors):
8	  - `packages/server/src/authz/sources.ts`: `ACL_SOURCES = [slack, github]`, `CHANNEL_READ_IDENTITIES = [slack]`
9	  - `packages/server/src/authz/acl-sync.ts`: hardcodes `runSlackAclSyncTick` + `runGithubAclSyncTick`
10	  - `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/sender-identity.ts`: `switch (platform)` Slack only
11	- Connectors *can* own `AclSourceDef` + normalizers (`slack-identity.ts`, `github-identity.ts`) but server must import them by hand.
12	- `ConnectorDefinition` does NOT declare ACL; no `aclSupport` on connector class.
13	- Chat transport works for telegram/whatsapp/discord/teams/gchat.
14	- Transcript capture stores raw `author_id` but `author_entity_id` is null for non-Slack because `buildSenderIdentity` returns null (unit test asserts telegram → null).
15	- Identity modules hand list: github, slack, x only.
16	- Derived-artifact provenance: not built (out of scope).
17	- Multi-user social relay: not built (out of scope).
18	
19	### Product requirement from product owner
20	1. ACL must be **plug-in**: connectors easily register; clean cut remove deprecated hand lists/ticks/switches (no shims).
21	2. **Telegram etc. must work**: know which chat user is which person (`author_entity_id` / entity_identities).
22	
23	## Proposed design
24	
25	### ConnectorAuthzModule (SDK or connectors package)
26	```
27	{
28	  key: string  // matches connector/platform key
29	  source?: AclSourceDef           // resource membership ACL
30	  aclSupport: 'none' | 'full'     // no 'partial' in v1
31	  channelRead?: ChannelReadIdentity  // chat group gates
32	  senderIdentity?: {
33	    build(sender: { teamId?, authorId?, isBot }): SenderIdentitySpec | null
34	  }
35	  syncAccessGraph?(ctx: AclSyncContext): Promise<
36	    { ok: true, resources: AccessResource[] } | { ok: false, reason: string }
37	  >
38	}
39	```
40	Register via side-effect `registerAuthzModule(m)` (mirror identity `registerConnector`).
41	
42	Server:
43	- `authz/registry.ts` — sole assembly; `aclSources()`, `channelReadIdentities()`, `buildSenderIdentity()` dispatch
44	- `load-authz-modules.ts` — explicit import list of modules (one file; core gates never name slack)
45	- `runAclSyncTick` — loop modules with `syncAccessGraph`; call existing `buildAccessGraph`; stamp freshness; fail-closed on ok:false
46	- DELETE: hand arrays in sources.ts, per-source tick orchestration, platform switch in sender-identity
47	
48	### Chat L1 (required for Telegram etc.) — NOT full group ACL
49	Per chat platform module:
50	- Namespace e.g. `telegram_user_id` (global numeric id, no team prefix)
51	- `senderIdentity.build` → mint/find `person` via existing `resolveSenderIdentity`
52	- WhatsApp: phone/wa_jid; Discord: snowflake; Teams/GChat: analogous
53	- Telegram group membership ACL (`syncAccessGraph`) **deferred** unless product requires private group channel gates
54	
55	### Phased clean cuts (no dual path)
56	
57	**PR1 — Chat L1 + sender registry** (unblocks "know who")
58	1. Introduce registry + `senderIdentity` dispatch; delete `switch (platform)`
59	2. Modules: telegram, whatsapp, discord, teams, gchat, slack (move slack branch)
60	3. Tests: unit per platform; integration telegram inbound → author_entity_id set; same user second message same entity
61	4. Flip sender-identity test (telegram must attribute, not null)
62	
63	**PR2 — ACL plug-in registry + move Slack/GitHub sync**
64	1. Slack/GitHub register full modules with `syncAccessGraph` (move fetch from server)
65	2. Generic tick only; DELETE slack-acl-sync.ts / github-acl-sync.ts server bodies
66	3. Credential ctx: server injects getCredential (bot/oauth/app) — workers never get durable secrets
67	4. Existing Slack/GitHub ACL integration tests must pass; git grep old tick names = 0
68	
69	**PR3 — Proof (optional same week)**
70	- One simple third source OR CI invariant: no connector names under authz/ except load file
71	
72	### Explicit non-goals
73	- AclExpr / partial ACL / Jira issue-security
74	- derived_artifact_sources
75	- social relay / consent graph
76	- custom org-uploaded connector ACL
77	- Telegram Login Widget → $member (L3 account link) — optional later
78	- Unifying identity fact registry with authz in same PR (can share load file later)
79	
80	### Risks
81	1. Secret resolution when moving fetch into connector package (BYO vs install)
82	2. channelKeySql must stay byte-identical to TS builders
83	3. First stamp must not hide all data (not-graphed vs failed)
84	4. Event entity_ids linking required for resource gate (GitHub already stamps; new sources must)
85	
86	### Success criteria
87	- git grep runSlackAclSyncTick / ACL_SOURCES = [slack → zero after PR2
88	- Telegram message → author_entity_id non-null, stable person
89	- Adding a new chat L1 = one module file + one import line, zero gate SQL edits
90	- Adding a new membership ACL source = module with syncAccessGraph + import, zero acl-sync.ts edits

# Plan: Connector authz/identity plug-in (clean cut) + chat L1 (Telegram etc.)

## Context (verified against origin/main code)

### Today
- Generic ACL engine exists: `buildAccessGraph` → `$resource` + `member_of`, `authz_source_acl_state` (not-graphed / enforced full+fresh / stale fail-closed), channel + resource visibility compilers.
- **Hardcoded allowlists** (not auto-discovery from connectors):
  - `packages/server/src/authz/sources.ts`: `ACL_SOURCES = [slack, github]`, `CHANNEL_READ_IDENTITIES = [slack]`
  - `packages/server/src/authz/acl-sync.ts`: hardcodes `runSlackAclSyncTick` + `runGithubAclSyncTick`
  - `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/sender-identity.ts`: `switch (platform)` Slack only
- Connectors *can* own `AclSourceDef` + normalizers (`slack-identity.ts`, `github-identity.ts`) but server must import them by hand.
- `ConnectorDefinition` does NOT declare ACL; no `aclSupport` on connector class.
- Chat transport works for telegram/whatsapp/discord/teams/gchat.
- Transcript capture stores raw `author_id` but `author_entity_id` is null for non-Slack because `buildSenderIdentity` returns null (unit test asserts telegram → null).
- Identity modules hand list: github, slack, x only.
- Derived-artifact provenance: not built (out of scope).
- Multi-user social relay: not built (out of scope).

### Product requirement from product owner
1. ACL must be **plug-in**: connectors easily register; clean cut remove deprecated hand lists/ticks/switches (no shims).
2. **Telegram etc. must work**: know which chat user is which person (`author_entity_id` / entity_identities).

## Proposed design

### ConnectorAuthzModule (SDK or connectors package)
```
{
  key: string  // matches connector/platform key
  source?: AclSourceDef           // resource membership ACL
  aclSupport: 'none' | 'full'     // no 'partial' in v1
  channelRead?: ChannelReadIdentity  // chat group gates
  senderIdentity?: {
    build(sender: { teamId?, authorId?, isBot }): SenderIdentitySpec | null
  }
  syncAccessGraph?(ctx: AclSyncContext): Promise<
    { ok: true, resources: AccessResource[] } | { ok: false, reason: string }
  >
}
```
Register via side-effect `registerAuthzModule(m)` (mirror identity `registerConnector`).

Server:
- `authz/registry.ts` — sole assembly; `aclSources()`, `channelReadIdentities()`, `buildSenderIdentity()` dispatch
- `load-authz-modules.ts` — explicit import list of modules (one file; core gates never name slack)
- `runAclSyncTick` — loop modules with `syncAccessGraph`; call existing `buildAccessGraph`; stamp freshness; fail-closed on ok:false
- DELETE: hand arrays in sources.ts, per-source tick orchestration, platform switch in sender-identity

### Chat L1 (required for Telegram etc.) — NOT full group ACL
Per chat platform module:
- Namespace e.g. `telegram_user_id` (global numeric id, no team prefix)
- `senderIdentity.build` → mint/find `person` via existing `resolveSenderIdentity`
- WhatsApp: phone/wa_jid; Discord: snowflake; Teams/GChat: analogous
- Telegram group membership ACL (`syncAccessGraph`) **deferred** unless product requires private group channel gates

### Phased clean cuts (no dual path)

**PR1 — Chat L1 + sender registry** (unblocks "know who")
1. Introduce registry + `senderIdentity` dispatch; delete `switch (platform)`
2. Modules: telegram, whatsapp, discord, teams, gchat, slack (move slack branch)
3. Tests: unit per platform; integration telegram inbound → author_entity_id set; same user second message same entity
4. Flip sender-identity test (telegram must attribute, not null)

**PR2 — ACL plug-in registry + move Slack/GitHub sync**
1. Slack/GitHub register full modules with `syncAccessGraph` (move fetch from server)
2. Generic tick only; DELETE slack-acl-sync.ts / github-acl-sync.ts server bodies
3. Credential ctx: server injects getCredential (bot/oauth/app) — workers never get durable secrets
4. Existing Slack/GitHub ACL integration tests must pass; git grep old tick names = 0

**PR3 — Proof (optional same week)**
- One simple third source OR CI invariant: no connector names under authz/ except load file

### Explicit non-goals
- AclExpr / partial ACL / Jira issue-security
- derived_artifact_sources
- social relay / consent graph
- custom org-uploaded connector ACL
- Telegram Login Widget → $member (L3 account link) — optional later
- Unifying identity fact registry with authz in same PR (can share load file later)

### Risks
1. Secret resolution when moving fetch into connector package (BYO vs install)
2. channelKeySql must stay byte-identical to TS builders
3. First stamp must not hide all data (not-graphed vs failed)
4. Event entity_ids linking required for resource gate (GitHub already stamps; new sources must)

### Success criteria
- git grep runSlackAclSyncTick / ACL_SOURCES = [slack → zero after PR2
- Telegram message → author_entity_id non-null, stable person
- Adding a new chat L1 = one module file + one import line, zero gate SQL edits
- Adding a new membership ACL source = module with syncAccessGraph + import, zero acl-sync.ts edits

/**
 * Connector-owned identity module contract.
 *
 * Each connector that mints identity namespaces exports one of these. It is the
 * connector's self-description of the identity vocabulary it owns: how to
 * normalize its namespaces, and which of them are backed by an event-recall
 * index. The server assembles every module into the ingest normalizer chain and
 * the recall-namespace set (see
 * server/src/identity/connector-identity-modules.ts) — core code never names a
 * specific connector.
 *
 * Adding a connector namespace is: define the constants + normalizer here,
 * list recall namespaces, and (if recall-indexed) ship the matching
 * `idx_events_metadata_<ns>` migration. A startup + CI invariant asserts the
 * recall-namespace set matches the physical indexes.
 */
export interface ConnectorIdentityModule {
  /** Connector/platform key (`slack`, `github`, `x`, …). */
  key: string;
  /**
   * Namespaces this connector owns that participate in read-time event recall.
   * Each MUST have a physical `idx_events_metadata_<ns>` partial index, or
   * recall seq-scans the events table. Enforced by a startup/CI invariant.
   */
  recallNamespaces: string[];
  /**
   * Normalize a value for one of this connector's namespaces. Returns
   * `undefined` when the namespace is not owned by this connector (the caller
   * chains to the next module, then to generic SDK hygiene). `null` means the
   * namespace IS owned but the value is invalid.
   */
  normalize(namespace: string, raw: string): string | null | undefined;
}

1	/**
2	 * Server-side assembly of connector-owned identity modules.
3	 *
4	 * This is the ONE place core code enumerates connectors for identity purposes.
5	 * Each connector owns its namespace constants + normalizers in its own package
6	 * (`@lobu/connectors/<key>-identity`); here we collect those self-descriptions
7	 * into the two things the server needs:
8	 *
9	 *   - `normalizeConnectorIdentityValue` — the ingest normalizer chain (each
10	 *     module gets first refusal via its `undefined` "not mine" sentinel; the
11	 *     caller falls back to generic SDK hygiene).
12	 *   - `CONNECTOR_RECALL_NAMESPACES` — the connector-contributed half of the
13	 *     event-recall namespace set. A startup + CI invariant asserts this exactly
14	 *     matches the physical `idx_events_metadata_<ns>` indexes.
15	 *
16	 * Adding a connector namespace: create/extend its `*-identity.ts` module in
17	 * `@lobu/connectors`, then add it to `CONNECTOR_IDENTITY_MODULES` below. Core
18	 * code never names a specific connector beyond this import list.
19	 */
20	
21	import type { ConnectorIdentityModule } from '@lobu/connectors/connector-identity-module';
22	import { githubIdentityModule } from '@lobu/connectors/github-identity';
23	import { slackIdentityModule } from '@lobu/connectors/slack-identity';
24	import { xIdentityModule } from '@lobu/connectors/x-identity';
25	
26	/** Every connector identity module the server wires in. */
27	export const CONNECTOR_IDENTITY_MODULES: readonly ConnectorIdentityModule[] = [
28	  githubIdentityModule,
29	  slackIdentityModule,
30	  xIdentityModule,
31	];
32	
33	/**
34	 * Normalize a value against every connector module, in registration order.
35	 * Returns the first module's result whose namespace it owns (`string` valid or
36	 * `null` invalid), or `undefined` when no connector owns the namespace — the
37	 * caller then applies generic SDK normalization.
38	 */
39	export function normalizeConnectorIdentityValue(
40	  namespace: string,
41	  raw: string,
42	): string | null | undefined {
43	  for (const module of CONNECTOR_IDENTITY_MODULES) {
44	    const result = module.normalize(namespace, raw);
45	    if (result !== undefined) return result;
46	  }
47	  return undefined;
48	}
49	
50	/**
51	 * The connector-contributed event-recall namespaces (deduped, insertion order).
52	 * Combined with the generic recall namespaces to form the full recall set.
53	 */
54	export const CONNECTOR_RECALL_NAMESPACES: readonly string[] = Array.from(
55	  new Set(CONNECTOR_IDENTITY_MODULES.flatMap((m) => m.recallNamespaces)),
56	);

All context verified against the working tree (which matches the plan's origin/main claims — I spot-checked each "Today" bullet). Review follows.

---

## 1. Verdict: **APPROVE WITH CHANGES**

PR1 is sound and product-critical. PR2 as specced contains a design error that would regress fail-closed granularity, and the registration mechanism is wrong for an authz surface. Both are fixable in the plan without changing its goals.

## 2. Confidence: **55/100** end-to-end clean cut as written

(PR1 alone, scoped to telegram + slack move: ~85. PR2 as specced: ~40 — the `syncAccessGraph` interface doesn't survive contact with `slack-acl-sync.ts`.)

## 3. Blockers

**B1 — Side-effect registration is fail-open on an authz gate.** The plan proposes `registerAuthzModule(m)` "mirror identity registerConnector" — but the identity wiring is *not* side-effect registration; it's a static import-list array (`packages/server/src/identity/connector-identity-modules.ts:27-31`). The plan mis-describes the pattern it claims to mirror. This matters because a null lookup means "no gate": `rowToChannelKey` returns null → gate drops/ungates (`packages/server/src/authz/acl-state.ts:147-154`), and `resolveRequesterByChatUserId` silently `continue`s (`packages/server/src/authz/channel-visibility.ts:111-112`). A mutable registry consulted before the load file runs makes Slack channels silently ungated — no error, just leakage. Keep the current shape: a static array assembled at module init in one file (which is exactly what `sources.ts` already is). The clean cut is *adding dispatch for sender identity and sync*, not swapping static assembly for temporal-coupled registration. Also collides with the repo's static-import invariant (AGENTS.md).

**B2 — `syncAccessGraph(ctx) → {ok, resources}` cannot express the real sync contract.** The actual Slack sync is: per-connection atomic fail-closed with `markConnectionAclFailed` (`packages/server/src/authz/slack-acl-sync.ts:89-103, 250-260`); per-team graph builds (`:161-248`); a load-bearing distinction between definitively-unreadable channels (empty-member reconcile → revoke stale edges, `:191-211`) and transient errors (whole connection fails closed); bot-member filtering (`:213-220`); and a BYO self-heal that *writes* `external_tenant_id` back to `connections` after `auth.test` (`:364-400`). A flat `{ok, resources}` return loses per-connection failure stamping and the transient-vs-terminal distinction — that's a fail-closed regression, which is a hard repo invariant. And "server injects getCredential" (plan line 66) is off by an order of magnitude: `resolveSlackBotIdentity` is ~130 lines with three fallback paths needing the install store, secret store, orgContext, and DB (`:273-403`).
